content.text:
I've saved the revised `finding.json` with `accepted: true`. The finding stands but is narrower and better supported: about $285,468.20 a year in revenue from shipped lines that were never invoiced (q325), which is about $71,523.61 a year of margin at static cost.

**What I accepted from the challenge:**
- **One mechanism, not two.** I dropped the "dropped line vs. whole missed order" reading. 1,131 of the 1,135 orders with nothing invoiced had only one line (q385). Counter orders lose lines at the same rate whether they have one line or several: 1.1272% vs 1.1232% (q381). So lines drop out one at a time, at a rate set by the channel.
- **Keyers.** The challenger's test adjusts for channel and finds the spread across the 48 people who key orders is what chance alone would produce (q387). That replaces my raw range, which mixed in each keyer's share of counter orders.
- **The counter effect is real, not customer mix.** It holds for the same 5,520 customers ordering both ways: 1.1244% at the counter vs 0.1531% by email or phone (q394). It also holds within every trade, fulfilment type and month (q391, q395, q392).
- **Ruled out with this data:**
  - Invoice headers hiding the missing lines.
  - Late billing: every line is invoiced on its ship day.
  - Duplicate or zero-price lines.
  - Customers paying the missing amount through accounts receivable anyway.

  Counter goods paid for off the books, through a till or cash drawer that never reaches finance, stays open because that record isn't in the warehouse.
- **Special orders.** The 234 uninvoiced special-order lines ($341,631.34) have no warehouse record, so whether they physically shipped rests on the ERP alone (q409).
- **Collectability.** 79.98% of the $2.84M dates from 2016–2023, so most of it probably can't be collected (q424).

**Where I corrected the challenger:** Their revised conclusion put 2024's billable lines with active customers at $297,236.84. That's the whole of 2024; the active-customer part is $285,621.84 (q406). Adding the 2025 lines gives a near-term pool to bill of $556,936.66 (q412). I also ran one new query (q424) to compute two figures the challenger had only estimated: the 2016–2023 total ($2,271,977.00) and margin as a share of revenue (25.05%).

The recommended next step hasn't changed: check a sample of counter orders against the counter till or cash receipts, then set up a daily report of shipped lines with no invoice line. Because invoices are always raised on the ship day, that report would catch every case exactly.
